Background

The Green Climate Fund (“GCF”) is a multilateral fund established to make significant contributions to global efforts in combating climate change. It operates under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement, supporting developing countries in reducing greenhouse gas emissions and adapting to climate change impacts. The GCF is governed by a Board with equal representation from developed and developing countries and is managed by an independent Secretariat. The Secretariat develops investment policies that are submitted for technical review and guidance by the GCF Board’s Operations and Portfolio Committee (“OPC”) and eventual consideration and approval by the GCF Board. The independent Technical Advisory Panel (“iTAP”) advises the Board by providing technical assessments and advice on funding proposals. The Secretariat supports the Board, the OPC and the iTAP to ensure effective operations and decision-making.

GCF is seeking an Operations Consultant (“the Consultant”) to play a central role in facilitating the investment policies for consideration by the Board and OPC and the technical assessments of funding proposals by the iTAP. The iTAP and OPC work remotely, so the consultant will join the Office of the Chief Investment Officer (“OCIO”), which is the Secretariat’s technical interface for both bodies, at the GCF headquarters in Songdo, Incheon, Republic of Korea. The assignment is for an initial period of 240 days over 12 months with the possibility of renewal.
Role

Under the guidance of the Chair of the iTAP, the Consultant is responsible for coordination of iTAP technical assessments, managing the related documentation, conducting data analysis and providing policy-related analytical support to iTAP, and coordinating with various stakeholders. The Consultant also will support the Secretariat on investment policies and matters submitted to the OPC. The Consultant will provide data analysis and operational support to inform investment policy proposals and revisions under the direction of the Investment Operations Manager within the OCIO. The Consultant will report to the Investment Operations Manager on all administrative matters.
Duties and responsibilities
Data and analysis:
Conduct data analysis of iTAP assessments during its review period and engagement with the Board and Secretariat.
Review iTAP outcomes and investment criteria scoring to identify trends and inform quality improvements.
Manage, maintain and analyze the database of iTAP funding proposal assessments.
Gather and analyze data and evidence to support the preparation of investment policy proposals and revisions.
Provide other analytical support to iTAP as requested.
Policy and technical support:
Support the preparation of policy and Board documents, including background analysis, research, drafting inputs, and supporting materials.
Prepare policy and technical presentations and supporting materials for Secretariat, OPC and Board audiences.
Lead editorial support for iTAP-related Board documents and reports.
Support Secretariat consultations with the OPC on policy and work programme items.
Provide other support to the OCIO on investment policy matters as requested.
Stakeholder engagement:
Maintain regular and appropriate communication between iTAP and Secretariat regarding the technical assessments of funding proposals.
Liaise with stakeholders, including the Board, accredited entities, and external consultants on iTAP-related matters.
Coordinate and prepare responses to queries from the Board, OPC and other stakeholders on policy proposals, in consultation with relevant colleagues.
iTAP coordination:
Organize internal meetings, technical sessions and public engagements (e.g., “Meet iTAP” sessions) of the iTAP.
Arrange briefings for iTAP members on relevant Board-approved policies and provide policy updates after each Board meeting.
Assist with iTAP appointments, onboarding, performance reviews, and contract management.
Support travel arrangements, logistics and procurement of consultants for iTAP members as needed.
Qualifications
Master’s degree with at least 3 years’ relevant experience, or bachelor’s degree with at least 5 years’ relevant experience.

Experience in project or programme coordination, data or policy analysis, and operational support, preferably within an international organization, development finance institution, or comparable context.
Strong organizational and detail-oriented skills; ability to multi-task and deliver quality work under pressure.
Strong interpersonal skills; ability to work collaboratively in multicultural teams.
Ability to exercise tact, discretion and integrity when dealing with confidential information.
Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.
Additional Desirable Skills
Familiarity with the GCF institutional structure, including the Board, OPC, iTAP and Secretariat.
Experience handling logistics for events, workshops, and Board meetings.
Familiarity with climate change policy, environmental/social development, or technical assessments of projects.
Experience supporting performance reviews, recruitment, and onboarding processes.
Contract Period and Duty Station: 12 months/ GCF Headquarters in Songdo, Republic of Korea
